To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) a unidirectional Rw model tends to underestimate fluxes and a bidirectional χw model overestimates flux measurements; (2)
the Rw-only parameterization of the unidirectional non- stomatal resistance (Rn) model of Massad et al.(2010) underestimates NH3 fluxes, while its bidirectional counterpart overestimates flux.

the two non-stomatal parameterizations are qualitatively comparable and that the bidirectional approach has the advantage of being able to represent the full range of observed NH3 exchange, but that both models need further refinement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of semi-empirical parameterizations of non-stomatal NH3 exchange in air quality models.
the development and testing of parameterization schemes for non-stomatal NH3 exchange, with an emphasis on bidirectional models and their implementation in air quality models.
a better understanding of the non-stomatal pathway in the context of air quality modeling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neither the Rw-only model nor the χw-only model is able to reproduce all flux measurements, although the bidirectional model is more successful than the unidirectional one.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the two models perform similarly well, the unidirectional Rw model is more robust and should be preferred in air quality models for the time being.

a unidirectional Rw-only model with a modified temperature response parameter and a bidirectional χw model with a modified minimum Rw are both suitable for representing non-stomatal NH3 exchange in air quality models.
the bidirectional model, with the proposed modifications, is the preferred option, but that the unidirectional approach is more suitable for use in air quality models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the non-stomatal fluxes are small in comparison to stomatal fluxes and are therefore difficult to measure, they are still important for the overall accuracy of air quality models.

the bidirectional model is more robust than the unidirectional one and can better capture the variability of fluxes, but that the unidirectional approach can be useful in the absence of stomatal conductance measurements, and in cases where the bidirectional approach is too complex to implement.
, despite the differences in their underlying assumptions, both state-of-the-art non-stomatal parameterizations can be used in air quality models to improve predictions of bidirectional NH3 fluxes.
